rationale: The last paused question needs a valid predicate before it can be closed, and its own probe previously used the broken configuration index accessor. This submission requests a repeated measurement that reads only the atomically published configuration content and the log store, twenty-five identical upgrade rounds with one admission per round, so the controller can decide both bounded propagation and the sharper question of a node holding an old membership while its own log already contains the configuration entry. The question stays paused rather than closed: the local run is native feedback, so the disposition is left open until the controller's receipt exists.

limitations: Answered for the reproduced scenario: with a valid predicate (published configuration content plus log store contents, never the broken index accessor), all nodes of the upgrade scenario reached the new membership and no node was observed holding the old membership while its log contained the configuration entry.
Native local run of the requested harness (not retained evidence): 25 of 25 rounds converged, with per-round maximum wait 0-5ms and any_lag_with_entry false in every round.

Not explained and not attributed: the earlier local observation that the captured TestRaft_ProtocolVersion_Upgrade_2_3 failed with a peer mismatch in about two of three isolated runs. Under instrumentation the same scenario converges in milliseconds, so the cause remains unknown rather than resolved.
The earlier probe for this question used GetConfiguration().Index() as its predicate; that accessor returns a constant zero, so its readings were invalid and are superseded by this measurement.
resume_conditions: Resume when the controller has executed the requested repeated probe, so the answer rests on a retained receipt rather than the native local run.

Resume earlier if a source or execution explains why the captured TestRaft_ProtocolVersion_Upgrade_2_3 failed locally in about two of three isolated runs while the instrumented scenario converges in milliseconds.

scope.description: Twenty-five repetitions of the captured upgrade scenario (protocol-2 pair plus a protocol-3 joiner) on in-memory clusters, each round following one AddVoter of the joiner and polling every 5ms for up to 3s for the published configuration content to include the joiner, then recording per node whether the entry is in its log store while its published content is still old.
assumptions: MakeCluster(2, protocol 2) plus a merged MakeClusterNoBootstrap(1, protocol 3) and AddVoter of the joiner reproduce the captured scenario, with the future's index identifying the configuration entry.

The atomically published configuration content is what GetConfiguration returns and what the captured cluster assertion compares; the configuration index accessor is excluded because it returns a constant zero.
Five-millisecond polling with a 3s window is dense enough to distinguish prompt propagation from a multi-second stall.
Every round is a fresh cluster, so rounds do not share state.
excluded: The configuration index accessor, which is covered by a separate finding.
Network transport behaviour, crashes and restarts.
Any claim about the captured test's earlier local failures, which this probe does not reproduce.

experiment.prefix: Built with captured test facilities and real producers only: per round a protocol-2 pair is bootstrapped, a protocol-3 single node is created without bootstrap, merged and fully connected, and the leader adds that node through AddVoter, whose future index identifies the configuration entry. The harness emits one config_round_probe_start per round with the iteration, entry index and cluster size, then one config_round_start per node with the starting published content and log store last index. It polls the atomically published content of every node every 5ms for up to 3s, records when each node first shows the joiner, and finally emits per-node config_node_result events carrying whether the entry is present in that node's log store together with its published content, log store last index, applied index and commit index, plus one config_round_end carrying all_converged, any_lag_with_entry, the maximum wait and the window. No storage is pre-filled and no production code is modified.
experiment.responsibility: Propagation of a committed configuration entry into the atomically published configuration content on every node of the captured upgrade scenario, and the duty of the log store to hold the entry that content is derived from.

comparisons.description: Every node's published configuration includes the joining voter within the 3s window, i.e. the committed configuration entry propagates to every node's visible membership.
No node published the old membership while its own log store already held the configuration entry, which is the 'stale configuration state' signature this question asks about.
